title: Determining Volumes by Slicing
lead: A solid is cut into thin slices perpendicular to an axis, each slice’s volume estimated from its cross-section, and the estimates summed into a Riemann sum whose limit is an integral. For a solid of revolution the cross-sections are disks, or washers where the solid has a cavity, about either axis or another line.
objectives: Determine the volume of a solid by integrating a cross-section (the slicing method).
Find the volume of a solid of revolution using the disk method.
Find the volume of a solid of revolution with a cavity using the washer method.
summary_html:
• Definite integrals can be used to find the volumes of solids. Using the slicing method, we can find a volume by integrating the cross-sectional area.
  • For solids of revolution, the volume slices are often disks and the cross-sections are circles. The method of disks involves applying the method of slicing in the particular case in which the cross-sections are circles, and using the formula for the area of a circle.
  • If a solid of revolution has a cavity in the center, the volume slices are washers. With the method of washers, the area of the inner circle is subtracted from the area of the outer circle before integrating.

exercises.prompt: Use the slicing method to derive the formula $V=\frac{1}{3}\pi r^{2}h$ for the volume of a circular cone.

answer.solution: Place the cone with its vertex at the origin and its axis along the $x$-axis, so that its base, a circle of radius $r$, stands at $x=h.$ The cross-sections perpendicular to the $x$-axis are circles, and by similar triangles the radius of the one at $x$ is $\frac{r}{h}x,$ so $A(x)=\pi\left(\frac{rx}{h}\right)^{2}.$ Then $V=\int_{0}^{h}\pi\frac{r^{2}}{h^{2}}x^{2}\,dx=\frac{\pi r^{2}}{h^{2}}\cdot\frac{h^{3}}{3}=\frac{1}{3}\pi r^{2}h.$
answer.hint: Use similar triangles, as in Example 6.6.

exercises.prompt: Derive the formula for the volume of a sphere using the slicing method.

answer.solution: Center the sphere of radius $r$ at the origin and slice it perpendicular to the $x$-axis. The cross-section at $x$, for $-r\le x\le r,$ is a disk of radius $\sqrt{r^{2}-x^{2}},$ so $A(x)=\pi(r^{2}-x^{2}).$ Then $V=\int_{-r}^{r}\pi(r^{2}-x^{2})\,dx=\pi\left[r^{2}x-\frac{x^{3}}{3}\right]_{-r}^{r}=\pi\left(2r^{3}-\frac{2r^{3}}{3}\right)=\frac{4}{3}\pi r^{3}.$

exercises.prompt: Use the slicing method to derive the formula for the volume of a cone.

answer.solution: Place the cone with its vertex at the origin and its axis along the $x$-axis, so that its base, a circle of radius $r$, stands at $x=h.$ The cross-sections perpendicular to the $x$-axis are circles, and by similar triangles the radius of the one at $x$ is $\frac{r}{h}x,$ so $A(x)=\pi\left(\frac{rx}{h}\right)^{2}.$ Then $V=\int_{0}^{h}\pi\frac{r^{2}}{h^{2}}x^{2}\,dx=\frac{\pi r^{2}}{h^{2}}\cdot\frac{h^{3}}{3}=\frac{1}{3}\pi r^{2}h.$

exercises.prompt: Use the slicing method to derive the formula for the volume of a tetrahedron with side length $a.$

answer.solution: Stand the regular tetrahedron of side $a$ on one face and measure $x$ down from its top vertex along the altitude, whose length is $H=a\sqrt{2/3}.$ The cross-section at $x$ is an equilateral triangle similar to the base, of side $s=\frac{a}{H}x,$ so $A(x)=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{4}s^{2}=\frac{\sqrt{3}a^{2}}{4H^{2}}x^{2}.$ Then $V=\int_{0}^{H}\frac{\sqrt{3}a^{2}}{4H^{2}}x^{2}\,dx=\frac{\sqrt{3}a^{2}H}{12}=\frac{\sqrt{3}a^{2}}{12}\cdot a\sqrt{\frac{2}{3}}=\frac{\sqrt{2}}{12}a^{3}=\frac{a^{3}}{6\sqrt{2}}.$ (With $a=4$ this is $\frac{32}{3\sqrt{2}},$ the answer to exercise 65.)

exercises.prompt: Use the disk method to derive the formula for the volume of a trapezoidal cylinder.

answer.solution: The solid a trapezoid sweeps when it is revolved about its long side is a frustum of a cone: take the trapezoid bounded by the $x$-axis, the lines $x=0$ and $x=h,$ and the line $y=r_{1}+\frac{r_{2}-r_{1}}{h}x,$ and revolve it about the $x$-axis. Each slice is a disk of radius $y,$ so $V=\int_{0}^{h}\pi\left[r_{1}+\frac{r_{2}-r_{1}}{h}x\right]^{2}dx.$ With $u=r_{1}+\frac{r_{2}-r_{1}}{h}x,$ $du=\frac{r_{2}-r_{1}}{h}dx,$ this is $\frac{\pi h}{r_{2}-r_{1}}\int_{r_{1}}^{r_{2}}u^{2}\,du=\frac{\pi h}{3}\cdot\frac{r_{2}^{3}-r_{1}^{3}}{r_{2}-r_{1}}=\frac{\pi h}{3}(r_{1}^{2}+r_{1}r_{2}+r_{2}^{2}).$ When $r_{1}=r_{2}=r$ it is $\pi r^{2}h,$ the volume of a cylinder.

exercises.prompt: Explain when you would use the disk method versus the washer method. When are they interchangeable?

answer.solution: Use the disk method when the region being revolved reaches the axis of revolution along the whole interval, so every slice is a solid disk of radius $f(x)$ and area $\pi[f(x)]^{2}.$ Use the washer method when the region is bounded away from the axis by a second curve $g(x)$ (or the axis is a line apart from the region), so every slice is a disk with a hole and its area is $\pi[(f(x))^{2}-(g(x))^{2}].$ They are interchangeable when the inner radius is zero: with $g(x)=0$ the washer formula is the disk formula. And a washer volume can always be found as the difference of two disk volumes, the solid swept by the outer curve less the solid swept by the inner one.
